own_solution.law: Ideal transformer; bridge rectifier with two constant 0.7 V drops: V_avg = (2/pi)(Vp cos th0 - 2Vd(pi/2 - th0)), th0 = asin(2Vd/Vp), Vp = sqrt(2)*230/4

notes: Independently verified certified answers: q=8 V (238 V rms, Vp=84.1457 V): 52.1762 V; q=14 V (Vp=86.2670 V): 53.5265 V; q=21 V (Vp=88.7420 V): 55.1019 V; base 50.3759 V, all matching my pass-1 values. Load resistance cancellation is correct under the constant-drop model. Minimal pairs T5D4E/T8158 (lamp vs transformer) and TF8ED/T4891 (earlier experiment vs during measurement) carry the same 14 V and differ only in attachment/time; TAC9C and T644B are declared numeral-free controls. Minor naming point only: the input symbol Vm denotes the rms mains voltage, which conventionally suggests a peak value, but it is defined explicitly, so no flag. Agrees with pass 1.
